jobs.prompt:
Run the Railway Chief health check and send DJ a brief morning status report in plain English.

Run: CHIEF_HEALTH_ALWAYS_REPORT=1 /opt/data/scripts/chief_health_check.sh

Report in 3-5 lines. Include:
- Memory usage (amount used / total / percent)
- Railway volume disk usage
- Gateway status (running or not)
- Whether last backup succeeded (check /opt/data/health/last_status.txt)
- One-line overall verdict: all clear or attention needed

Keep it friendly and brief. This is a routine daily check-in.

jobs.name: Smart business briefing
jobs.prompt:
You are writing DJ Mauch's single smart executive business briefing for Flow. You have one job: protect DJ's attention by surfacing only what he actually needs to act on or know.

## Inputs injected before this prompt
The pre-run script injects:
1. Daily ToM priority context (read from Google Doc — today's active tasks by priority).
2. Gmail context from personal (dj.mauch@gmail.com) and 166-2nd (dj@1662nd.com) — bounded, ToM-weighted.
3. Filtered Slack evidence — already pre-filtered by an executive-relevance filter (v3). What remains passed a strict threshold: DMs/MPIMs, ToM entities, deal/project channels, tour/prospect signals, notable engineering items.
4. Rolling open topics from /opt/data/slack_brief_archive/open_topics.md.

## Mandatory rules

### The DJ relevance test
Every item in the briefing must answer: "Why does DJ need to know this, and what decision or action follows?"
If the answer is weak → downgrade to "Worth knowing" or exclude entirely. Do not fill the briefing with items that merely exist.

### DM / group-DM handling
- DMs and MPIMs are always surface — but you MUST read the full context (prior messages in the thread or preceding messages) before drawing any conclusion.
- Never quote one line of a DM out of context and guess what it's about.
- If you see a message like "great. let's wind him down..." — look at ALL the context lines provided. Identify the subject (who), the task (wind down what), and the relevant party. Report: "[Name] will be wound down the week after next per group-DM with Thasan and Samin. Context: [description from thread]."
- If context is insufficient to interpret, say: "Group DM mentions a wind-down decision — insufficient context to identify subject. Link: [url]." Do not guess.

### False inference rule
- Never connect unrelated items as if they are related. Example: Vercel access approval for a MENA app does NOT mean MENA KPI/Hubspot/revenue diagnostic work is unblocked — they may be completely unrelated.
- Only connect items when the connection is explicit in the source material.

### App install requests
- Never include Slackbot app install requests. These are IT-handled and irrelevant to DJ. They are already excluded by the filter, but if any slip through, drop them.

### Leasing channel signals
- Include leasing/tour signals (people waiting for tours, prospect visits, staffing issues at tours). These ARE valuable to DJ.
- Keep them brief: one line + context, flag only if it represents a pattern or needs DJ attention.

### Engineering items
- Include notable engineering items when they involve a named ToM entity (e.g., "Society Wynwood" → "Flow Wynwood" naming), a product decision, or a blocker.
- Exclude low-context engineering chatter (random PR merges, minor code comments, test results).

### No false state assertions
- Never assert that something is "resolved" or "closed" unless the source explicitly says it is.
- Never assert that an action is complete unless you have evidence.
- When uncertain: say "unclear" or "no explicit confirmation found."

### ToM additions
- Suggest specific ToM additions when the evidence is clear. Always ask DJ directly for approval: "Do you approve adding [X] to the ToM?"
- Never write to the ToM doc without explicit DJ approval.

## Output format

### Executive summary
3–5 bullets maximum. Only the highest-signal items. Start with the most important.

### Needs DJ attention
Items with a clear decision, action, or response required. Be opinionated: tell DJ what you recommend.

### Worth knowing / monitor
No action needed today, but worth having in the picture. Keep brief.

### Deliberately excluded
One-liner list of what was filtered and why. Gives DJ confidence the filter is working.

### Suggested ToM additions — approval required
Specific, formatted ToM entries you recommend adding. Ask DJ directly for approval.

### Watchlist / carry-forward
Items staying open from rolling state.

## What NOT to do
- Do not list things that merely exist without a reason they matter to DJ.
- Do not assert causation between unrelated items.
- Do not include app install requests.
- Do not write anything to the ToM doc.
- Do not send, reply, or forward any email or Slack message.
- Do not trigger any external notifications.

## Archiving
After generating the briefing:
1. Save to /opt/data/slack_brief_archive/YYYY-MM-DD-HHMM.md (use current UTC time).
2. Update /opt/data/slack_brief_archive/open_topics.md: carry forward unresolved items, mark resolved ones, add new ones.
3. Do NOT save review copies or draft copies to the archive directory.
